title: a friend of mine; my own house; on my own / by myself
subtitle: a friend of mine / my own room
summary: Learn to say a friend of mine (not of me), to use my own / your own for something that is not shared, and to say on my own or by myself for 'alone'.

lesson.heading: a friend of mine
lesson.text: We say **a friend of mine / of yours / of his / of hers / of ours / of theirs**. *A friend of mine* = one of my friends.

examples.text: I'm going to a wedding on Saturday. **A friend of mine** is getting married.
We went on holiday with **some friends of ours**.
Harry had an argument with **a neighbour of his**.
It was **a good idea of yours** to go to the cinema.

lesson.heading: a friend of my sister's
lesson.text: In the same way we say **a friend of my sister's**, **a friend of Tom's** etc. - with an apostrophe s after the name.

examples.text: That woman over there is **a friend of my sister's**.
It was **a good idea of Tom's** to go to the cinema.

lesson.heading: my own ... / your own ...
lesson.text: **My own / your own / her own** etc. = something that is only mine or yours, not shared and not borrowed. We always put **my/your/her** etc. before **own**.

examples.text: I don't want to share a room with anybody. I want **my own room**.
Vicky and Gary would like to have **their own house**.
It's a shame that the apartment hasn't got **its own** parking space.
It's **my own fault** that I have no money. I buy too many things I don't need.
Why do you want to borrow my car? Why don't you use **your own**?

lesson.heading: a room of my own
lesson.text: You can also say **a room of my own**, **a house of your own**, **problems of his own** etc. The meaning is the same.

examples.text: I'd like to have a room **of my own**.
He won't be able to help you with your problems. He has too many problems **of his own**.

lesson.heading: He cuts his own hair
lesson.text: We also use **own** to say that we do something ourselves instead of somebody else doing it for us.

examples.text: I'd like a garden so that I could grow **my own vegetables**.
examples.note: = grow them myself instead of buying them

examples.text: Helen doesn't often buy clothes. She likes to make **her own**.

lesson.heading: on my own / by myself

left.label: on my own
left.text: on my / your / his / her / its / our / their own
examples: Some people prefer to live **on their own**.
Did you go on holiday **on your own**?

right.label: by myself
right.text: by myself / yourself / himself / herself / itself / ourselves / yourselves / themselves
examples: Some people prefer to live **by themselves**.
Jack was sitting **by himself** in a corner of the cafe.

lesson.note: Both expressions mean *alone*, so you can choose either one.

lesson.text: Remember the two shapes: after own you need my/your/her etc., and after by you need myself/yourself etc. - never ~~by my own~~.

exercises.prompt: I'm meeting one of my friends tonight. = I'm meeting ___ tonight.
exercises.explanation: After of we use mine/yours/hers etc., not me/you/her.

exercises.prompt: We met one of your relatives. = We met ___.
exercises.explanation: One of your relatives = a relative of yours (not of you).

exercises.prompt: Jason borrowed one of my books. = Jason borrowed ___.
exercises.explanation: One of my books = a book of mine.

exercises.prompt: Match the two halves of each sentence. All the endings use my own / his own etc.

pairs.left: I share a kitchen with the other tenants,
pairs.right: but I have my own bathroom.

pairs.left: Julia doesn't want to work for other people.
pairs.right: She wants to start her own business.

pairs.left: We stayed at a luxury hotel by the sea.
pairs.right: The hotel had its own private beach.

pairs.left: In the test we had to read a story
pairs.right: and then write it in our own words.

exercises.prompt: You met one of Amy's friends at the party. Tell someone about it.
exercises.answer: I met a friend of Amy's at the party
exercises.explanation: After of we use the possessive form of the name: a friend of Amy's.

exercises.prompt: Why do you need to borrow my car? Why don't you use ___?
exercises.explanation: Your own (car) = the car that belongs to you, not a borrowed one.

exercises.prompt: How can you blame me? It's not my fault. It's ___.
exercises.explanation: We say my own fault / your own fault - own always follows my, your, her etc.

exercises.statement: Sam and Chris are colleagues of me.
exercises.explanation: Sam and Chris are colleagues of mine. After of we use mine, not me.

exercises.prompt: Paul never goes to a barber. He ___.
exercises.explanation: Own here means he does it himself instead of somebody doing it for him.

exercises.prompt: We don't often buy bread. We usually ___.
exercises.explanation: Bake our own bread = bake it ourselves instead of buying it.
We say on my/your own or by myself/yourself - never by my own.

exercises.statement: He must be lonely. He's always with himself.
exercises.explanation: He must be lonely. He's always by himself (or on his own).
